mission: Common area. Torin tells an NSW battle story with self-deprecating warmth. Ben watches the structure underneath: I decided, I acted, I bore the cost. Every story Torin has told has the same architecture. The laughter is warm and perfectly timed and Ben has seen this before — he wonders when he started analysing Torin's laughter, and then when he stopped doing it with Jacen too late. Across the common area, Ben's eyes find Desh's. Per R13, the single explicit Jacen naming lands here: one of them thinks or says the words 'Like Jacen.' A single sentence. The line the book has been saving. It lands; it is not underlined; the scene does not rest on it. R10 advances. H15 resolves. In the same scene: per D7 counter-current 4, Torin — mid-story — interrupts himself to pour a second cup for Sera before she can reach for it. No framing. No warmth announced. Sera takes it. The moment passes. It is the kind of thing the man who will walk into the caldera would not stop to do, and Ben files it without resolving it.
why_now: The Ch 11 conversation with Desh planted the pattern; the Ch 17 doorway line delivered the cadence; the Ch 17 s2 group-fracture scene left the question in the room. The recognition crystallises here because the evidence is a laugh and a story — two things Ben has been watching and not cataloguing. The chapter is the Second Pinch Point, and the name belongs to this moment or to no moment: per R13, this is the single-naming budget for the book's surface.
conflict: Ben has been watching Torin for chapters without naming what he is watching. The laugh is perfect, the stories are warm, the cadence is Jacen's. Then Torin, without transition, pours Sera a cup of caf — a small kindness Ben cannot fit inside the pattern he has just named. The scene asks Ben to hold two things at once: the pattern that is real, and the gesture that complicates it. Neither resolves the other.
turning_point: Ben catches the pattern in Torin's stories. The Jacen name arrives — once, quietly, between Ben and Desh. Seconds later, Torin pours Sera the second cup, and Ben has no framework ready to hold both.
opening_hook: Torin is laughing at something Desh said. The laugh is perfect — warm, easy, generous. Ben wonders when he started analysing Torin's laughter for authenticity, and then he wonders why he stopped doing it with Jacen too late.
closing_hook: The scene closes with Torin still mid-story, Sera cradling the second cup, and Ben carrying a name he now has and a gesture he cannot place
emotional_trajectory: Watchful analysis -> dawning recognition -> the name landing once -> the unresolved weight of Torin's cup-pouring

stakes.personal: Ben watching a path he has seen before, on a person he has come to rely on, and holding a gesture that refuses the simplicity of the pattern
stakes.interpersonal: Ben and Desh's shared recognition — the GAG-forged bond doing the work it was forged for; Torin's gesture toward Sera rendering both of them harder to categorise
stakes.external: Torin is the group's strongest combatant and may be becoming its greatest threat — but the threat is not simple, and the book refuses to let Ben simplify it
